subject: Guest access permissions and alternative join link for hybrid demo
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@fintechco.com>, IT Admin <it-admin@fintechco.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Guest access permissions and alternative join link for hybrid demo

Hi Jordan / team,

Thanks again for scheduling the product walkthrough for next Tuesday (Apr 5). A quick heads-up — our calendar invite appears to have triggered your org's SSO/guest block when we added an external Zoom organizer. Jordan, you mentioned your security team prevents external Zoom hosts from joining without an approved SSO assertion. We want to avoid any last-minute join issues for the demo.

Can you confirm whether your IT team can:
- Allow a single external Zoom host for the event (alex_martinez@redwood.com), or
- Prefer that we provide a Google Meet link instead so participants authenticate via your Google SSO (recommended if Zoom external hosts are blocked).

If Meet is preferred we can:
- Send an updated calendar invite with Meet as the primary join method and include a Zoom fallback link in the description,
- Attach a short SSO checklist for your IT (attached) to help test before the demo.

I've attached a stubbed ICS (demo-invite.ics) and sso-checklist.pdf for your IT. If helpful, Tessa (cc'd) can build a dual-link invite that puts both links in the event description and pins the organizer to our Redwood account while listing your attendees normally.

Goal: zero friction for attendees — please let us know the path your team prefers and if IT wants to test a join ahead of time.

Thanks,

Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: demo-invite.ics (stub), sso-checklist.pdf (stub)

From: Jordan Lee <jordan@fintechco.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, IT Admin <it-admin@fintechco.com>

On Thu, Apr 29, 2027 at 9:12 AM Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Jordan / team,
>
> Thanks again for scheduling the product walkthrough for next Tuesday (Apr 5). A quick heads-up — our calendar invite appears to have triggered your org's SSO/guest block when we added an external Zoom organizer...

Thanks Alex — appreciate the proactive note. Our security policy blocks external Zoom hosts that don't authenticate via our enterprise SSO (we use Google Workspace SSO integration).

Short answer: our IT will not enable external Zoom hosts for calendar events. We can either:
- Use a Google Meet link (preferred), or
- If Redwood needs Zoom for specific features, provide Meet as the default and Zoom as a fallback link in the invite description; IT will ask attendees to use Meet unless explicitly needed.

I've looped in our IT Admin to coordinate testing.

—Jordan
Jordan Lee
Product Lead, FinTechCo
jordan@fintechco.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@fintechco.com>, IT Admin <it-admin@fintechco.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Guest access permissions and alternative join link for hybrid demo

Thanks Jordan — that helps.

Workaround proposal (keeps things simple for attendees):
1) I'll create a single calendar event with Google Meet as the primary join link (so your SSO flow will work for authenticated users).
2) In the event description I'll add a secondary Zoom join URL (Zoom will be listed as a fallback with a short note: "Use Zoom only if you cannot join via Google Meet").
3) I'll attach an updated ICS (demo-invite.ics) that references the Meet link and include the sso-checklist.pdf for IT to validate.
4) Note on organizer/host controls: the event organizer will remain Alex (redwood). For Zoom fallback we can set an alternate Redwood co-host if needed, but that fallback won't be able to bypass your SSO — hence making Meet primary avoids host-blocks.

Alex — creating the dual-link event now and will send the updated invite. IT Admin: can you confirm if you'd like a PST dial-in number included in the description and any internal test accounts we should expect?

Tessa Morgan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
tessa_morgan@redwood.com

Attachment: demo-invite.ics (updated stub)

From: IT Admin <it-admin@fintechco.com>

Hi Tessa / Alex,

Thanks — we received the updated ICS with the Meet link and the SSO checklist. We'll run a quick join test from a standard employee account (no admin privileges) at 3:30pm PT and let you know if anything pops. Please include a PST dial-in (toll) number in the event description so our field folks can call if needed.

Also: for the Zoom fallback, please flag in the description that external hosts may be blocked; we'll instruct attendees to use Meet unless otherwise directed.

We appreciate the dual-link approach — should avoid the friction.

Regards,
IT Admin
FinTechCo IT Security
it-admin@fintechco.com

P.S. If you need us to whitelist a Redwood host for a future event, open a support ticket and we'll evaluate (not guaranteed).
